summary: How antisemitic right-wing media and street-fighting leagues in interwar France, inflamed by the Stavisky fraud scandal, led to the deadly far-right riot that tried to storm the Chamber of Deputies in Paris on 6 February 1934.

evidence.note: Dreyfus affair opens the story as the origin of the French far right (host says 1884; actual arrest 1894)
long segment on the right-wing press ecosystem and its growing antisemitism
infighting between Radicals, Socialists and Communists and the 1924 and 1932 elections
biography of Maurras and his Action Francaise newspaper and league
Croix-de-Feu veterans league, its structure and role in the riot
Stavisky's fraud scheme with municipal pawn shops and fake bonds
the 6 February 1934 march on the Palais Bourbon, police gunfire and deaths
fate of the rioters under Vichy and Maurras's 1945 life sentence

notes: Covered span ends at 1945 for the Vichy-era fates of the leaders and Maurras's sentencing, a short (about 3 minute) segment; end could arguably be 1936 (Popular Front). Comparisons to January 6 2021 and Epstein are comparisons, so reaches_present is false. Host dates the Dreyfus arrest to 1884; history and the 1894 date used here.
